paragraphs: Shimon Achi Azariah. (A Tanna of the Mishnah).
According to Maimonides in his [introduction to Zera'im](https://www.sefaria.org/Rambam_Introduction_to_the_Mishnah.22.4), he was the uncle of R' Elazar ben Azariah.

His brother Azariah was also a great Torah scholar, as in [Yevamot 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.16a.5), where R' Dosa ben Harkinas called him "our colleague." Azariah engaged in commerce and provided for his brother Shimon so that he could study Torah, and therefore Shimon was called by his brother's name, as in [Sotah 21a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.21a.16), where they said, "Not like Shimon Achi Azariah" (and [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Sotah.21a.16.1) explains that he studied Torah through his brother's support, so that his brother would share in the merit of his learning).[^3]
He is mentioned in [Mishnah Zevachim 1:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Zevachim.1.2), where he disagrees with R' Eliezer and Yose ben Choni.
And in [Tahorot 8:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Tahorot.8.7) [supplied 8:6] he disagrees with Rabbi Eliezer (ר״א) and Rabbi Yehoshua.[^1]
And in [Semachot 3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Tractate_Semachot.3.3) the text reads "Shimon ben Achi Azariah," and Hyman says that the word "ben" must be deleted.[^2]

And in [Yalkut, Chukat, remez 763](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Torah.763.1) [supplied 753], he debated with Rabbi Eliezer (ר״א) and Rabbi Yehoshua, and Rabbi Yehoshua answered him: "Shimon my brother, I cannot refute you," and Hyman says this is from the lost Sifrei Zuta.[^4]

notes.text: [Hyman’s printed notice](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=322) gives Tahorot 8:7, Semachot 3:3 and Yalkut Chukat 763. The supplied Hebrew gives Tahorot 8:6 and Yalkut 753. The linked passages contain the relevant wording.
The consulted Semachot text reads “Shimon ben Achi Azariah.” Hyman says that ben must be deleted. The Hebrew keeps the variant as supplied.

Maimonides calls Shimon Elazar ben Azariah’s uncle. Rashi explains that Azariah supported Shimon and shared the merit of his study. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3425&lang=en) also discusses both traditions.
The Yalkut has Rabbi Yehoshua say, “Shimon my brother, I cannot refute you.” Hyman attributes the passage to the lost Sifrei Zuta.
